`imbue/minds_evals/templates/` is type-checked. Those files run inside the verifier container rather than the dev process, and three of them (`tests/verifier/gates/checks.py`, `tests/verifier/quality/wordiness.py`, `outcome/checks.py`) import `rewardkit`, which the container installs via `uvx` -- so the whole directory was excluded from this project's `ty` config and checked nowhere. The rest are pure stdlib and were excluded only by association, including `tests/verifier/finalize.py`, which composes every trial's final gated reward.

`harbor-rewardkit` joins the dev group so the type checker can resolve those imports. Nothing this project runs imports it; it exists for the checker alone, which is exactly what makes it easy to prune as unused. Two checks hold it in place. `imbue/minds_evals/rewardkit_pin_test.py` requires the dev-group pin to equal the one `templates/tests/verifier/test.sh` passes to `uvx`, so the version being checked is the version that grades trials. And `templates/` cannot quietly be excluded here again: `test_meta_ratchets.py` at the repo root requires the root workspace to type-check whatever a standalone project excludes, and the root excludes `templates/`, so excluding it here too fails that check.

This covers import and signature drift across those files, not their behaviour. The wiring they sit in -- `judge.toml`, `reward.toml`, `test.sh` ordering, the verifier Dockerfile -- is still only exercised by a real trial.
